sprint: Second Supabase 57014 — Root-Caused as a Real Client-Side Race, Not a Second RLS Gap
task: a direct follow-up right after the first schema.sql fix was applied, showing a real DevTools Network entry -- PATCH .../builder_projects 500 (Internal Server Error), 21.16s, unable to load any response data. Confirmed genuinely separate from the earlier RLS-subquery fix (builder_projects's own policies are plain owner_id checks with zero correlated subqueries). Root cause, traced to js/creatorProjectCache.js's Studio-side sibling: js/projectCache.js's drainPendingSync() -- the retry-forever cloud-sync loop -- has four independent triggers (boot, the browser's online event, a 60s interval, and a 2s debounce fired from every edit) with zero coordination between them. Two firing close together start overlapping drain cycles, each independently deciding the SAME pending record is due and both calling _attemptSync(id) concurrently -- two separate DB transactions racing to UPDATE the exact same row, the second blocking on the first's row lock until it commits; any real-world hiccup holding the first transaction open turns that ordinary sub-millisecond wait into a genuine, repeating statement-timeout, matching both the reported 21-second duration (queued behind a stuck lock) and the empty response body (a severed connection). Fixed with an in-flight guard (_drainInFlightPromise, set synchronously before any await so even two calls in the same tick correctly de-duplicate) in js/creatorProjectCache.js -- the Studio side changed in this ship; the identical byte-for-byte fix already landed in js/projectCache.js. Verified via a dedicated Playwright reproduction (a real test-mock bug caught along the way -- a delayed fake network .then() that never returned a real Promise, silently defeating the artificial delay -- was found and fixed before the real fix could be properly proven): two synchronous calls return the exact same promise; three overlapping triggers within a slowed fake network window produce exactly ONE real DB call, not two; the record still settles correctly; a later project still drains on its own fresh cycle; two records pending at once both still push exactly once each. Full regression across every existing Cloud-Primary Project Storage Playwright suite (Phase 1-6, both surfaces) and both goldenBuild.js suites passes unchanged. See CLAUDE.md's own entry for the full account.
